Q: How can I configure a Gradle plugin externally to the build? A:

For the specific case of working with linked working trees, version 2.5.3 of gradle-git-properties fixed the underlying issue.

Upgrading the plugin to 2.5.3 or later will mean that the workaround can be removed.

Q: JavaFX and OpenJDK A:

Quick Summary

For all the details, see correct Answer by jewelsea. Here is a quick summary to directly address your Question's points.

OpenJFX versus OpenJDK

the alternative OpenJFX will only be fully integrated into OpenJDK in version 9.

OpenJFX is not integrated within the OpenJDK codebase. OpenJFX is a separate, optional library.

In 2026, OpenJFX is the open-source implementation of JavaFX, an official sub-project under the OpenJDK project. The project is co-managed by Gluon and Oracle. OpenJFX is under active development.

OpenJFX is delivered as a library, separate from the OpenJDK Java releases. Releases arrive on schedule, every six months, around the same time as the OpenJDK releases for Java. Version numbers are synchronized, with OpenJFX 25 and Java 25 being the current versions.

There has been recent discussion about delivering OpenJFX within every release of OpenJDK. But nothing official has happened.

OpenJDK publishes only source-code, not binaries nor installers (except for some early-access builds). You can obtain binaries/installers as JDK or JRE products from any of several vendors. All are high-quality, and thoroughly tested. Most of these JDK/JRE products are based largely, if not entirely, on the OpenJDK codebase. These vendors include:

  • SAP
  • BellSoft
  • IBM
  • RedHat
  • Azul Systems
  • Adoptium of the Eclipse Foundation
  • Oracle
  • Amazon
  • Microsoft
  • … and others.

To be clear: Anyone is free to write their own implementation of the Java specifications. In the past, some organizations did write their own original implementation. But nowadays most JDK/JRE products are based on the OpenJDK codebase.

JDK/JRE + OpenJFK bundles

Some of those vendors choose to distribute an edition of their JDK/JRE products that bundles the OpenJFX library. I know of at least two such vendors:

  • Azul Systems, with their JDK FX & JRE FX products.
  • BellSoft, with their LibericaFX products.

You can install such bundled JDKs on your own computer for development. And you can install such bundled JREs on your users’ computer for deployment. Otherwise, you will need to bundle a copy of OpenJFX as part of your app.

Note that OpenJFX, as well as JDK/JRE products, contains native code. So if you distribute your apps containing OpenJFX and/or a JRE, you must make a build for every native platform such as macOS on ARM, macOS on Intel, Linux on ARM, Linux on x86, Linux on Power, etc.

OpenJFX + OpenJDK ≈ peanut butter + jelly

Is the JavaFX support in OpenJDK still so bad?

There is nothing bad about JavaFX with OpenJDK. As discussed above, OpenJFX (JavaFX) is actually a sub-project hosted at the OpenJDK project. OpenJFX is developed alongside the OpenJDK codebase, with coinciding releases.

Gluon and possibly other companies provide commercial support for OpenJFX if you so require.

OpenJFX + OpenJDK bundles for Linux

If so, are there any Linux distributions that already offer an OpenJFX package

Yes. The two vendors listed above provide bundles of their JDK/JRE products for Linux with OpenJFX. These products are based on the OpenJDK codebase.

  • Azul Systems offers JDK/JRE products bundled with OpenJFK for Linux, implementing the specifications for Java 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25 (all the LTS versions).
  • BellSoft does too.

Q: LibVLCSharp VideoView overflows bounds in AvaloniaUI A:

As a workaround, you can leverage the overlay window to draw the adornments yourself on a transparent background (where you see the video through the overlay).

Rounded corners, hover effects... could be drawn on this overlay, over the VideoView window, by placing that content between the <VideoView> tags, as in WPF

Q: scanf_s not enough arguments passed for format string(Visual Studio) A:

As the error message indicates, there is a missing argument in scanf_s("%s", st[i].name). According to the Annex K of the C Standard, you should pass the length of the destination array for a %s conversion. The char pointer should be followed by an extra argument of type rsize_t indicating the number of elements in the array pointed to by the previous argument:

K.3.5.3.2 The fscanf_s function

The fscanf_s function is equivalent to fscanf except that the c, s, and [ conversion specifiers apply to a pair of arguments (unless assignment suppression is indicated by a *). The first of these arguments is the same as for fscanf. That argument is immediately followed in the argument list by the second argument, which has type rsize_tand gives the number of elements in the array pointed to by the first argument of the pair.

K.3.5.3.4 The scanf_s function

The scanf_s function is equivalent to fscanf_s with the argument stdin interposed before the arguments to scanf_s.

The type rsize_t is identical to the type size_t but has a restricted range of 0 to RSIZE_MAX.

On the other hand, the Microsoft Documentation for this function differs on the type for the number of elements: it specifies in a highlighted note that reads:

The size parameter is of type unsigned, not size_t. Use a static cast to convert a size_t value to unsigned for 64-bit build configurations.

Therefore, if you want your program to compile with the Microsoft compiler, you should modify the code as:

        scanf_s("%s", st[i].name, (unsigned)sizeof(st[i].name));

But if you want the program to conform to the C Standard, the cast (unsigned) should be removed.

For this reason (among others), the functions from Annex K are not portable across architectures and are not even supported on many of them. Consider using standard, well defined functions such as scanf and pass the maximum number of bytes to read as:

        scanf("%9s", st[i].name);

You can disable the warning emitted by Microsoft Visual Studio about scanf by adding these lines before including <stdio.h>:

#ifdef _MSC_VER
#define _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS
#endif

Finally, note that you must check the return value of scanf, scanf_s and all related functions to detect invalid or missing input and avoid further undefined behavior. scanf will return 1 if a word was read into the name array and 0 or EOF otherwise.

Q: ggsankey entries for "no node" A:

Make sure you're not passing a dataframe that has any NAs to make_long(). In the results of make_long() that you're passing to ggplot, you should only have NAs for the next_x and next_node for the last x (earnings). The node column should not have any NAs.
